title: Hired at the Fern Dance Hall at fourteen
summary: A drummer gets him a dance hall job at $25-30 a week; his mother consents if Uncle George sees him home.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You say there were no other of the second generation jazz musicians in this young group that you led with? Not at that time.

Not at that time. I had not yet come in contact with anyone. This came later, after I played at this little theater down here. There was a drummer, who I must confess that my memory is just failing me a little bit at this point here, who was working at the Furn Dance Hall. And he met my father and told my father, he said, there is a very good position open at a dance hall. He says, and it would pay Ormond $25 or $30 a week. Well, I was only 14 years old at the time. And when he told me that, I said, gee, I said, I'd love to do it. So they said it would be from eight to one. So when I told my mother about it, she liked to flip, you know, going to work in a dance hall. Fourteen years old, I had just gone in long pants, because you know, in those days we used to wear short pants until we were 12, 13 years old. And I had just gone in the long pants. But my mother finally consented to let me go to work under one condition. My uncle, the brother of Durschmeed, his name was George Schmeed, which was another brother of my mother's. He was the night policeman down on Canal Street. And everybody knew him. He was about 6'2 and weighed about 350 pounds. And everybody knew him. They called him Smith or Schmeed or I don't know what they had, Corporal. They had all kind of names for him. So my mother says, well, as long as your Uncle George sees you home in the morning time, it's all right. So when it would come time to me to...

get off, my uncle would pass around the fern and he would see that I got on a streetcar and got home. So this was the only way that I was able to start playing at such an early age, especially in a place like a dance hall.
